title: Paradise Airlines 901A
summary: The Lockheed Constellation was on approach to Tahoe Valley Airport in a heavy snowstorm with very low visibility. The pilot decided to attempt a visual approach after spotting a break in clouds. The crew became disoriented, lost awareness of the aircraft's altitude and location while flying below minimum safe altitude in mountainous terrain, and crashed into a mountain pass.
probable_cause: Pilot's decision to continue a visual approach when visibility was too low due to clouds and snowstorms, followed by loss of situational awareness of the aircraft's altitude and location as it descended below safe minimums in mountainous terrain.

factors.evidence: Heavy snowstorm obscured visibility, clouds had obscured the tops of mountains in the vicinity
Aircraft flew below minimum safe altitude in mountainous terrain
Crew lost awareness of plane's location and altitude after visual reference was lost during descent
Pilot attempted to fly through a low mountain pass believing it led to Reno airport, causing premature descent
Aircraft crashed into the left shoulder of a mountain pass at Genoa Peak

events.text: Departing San Jose with 81 passengers and 4 crew; Weather Bureau forecast predicted unsuitable conditions but dispatcher approved departure
Pilot reported spotting a break in cloud cover, seeing the airport on south shore of lake, decided to proceed with visual approach
Pilots contacted ground agent stating they would arrive shortly and to prepare for passengers
Aircraft descended below minimum safe altitude in mountainous terrain while crew became spatially disoriented
Crew attempted to navigate through a low mountain pass believed to lead to Reno, descending into mountainous terrain in heavy snow
Aircraft crashed into the left shoulder of a mountain pass at Genoa Peak, destroying the fuselage into tiny pieces
